en: Itivuttaka 57: Tikanipāta, Paṭhamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. Thereupon, the venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him: “Venerable sir, it was said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, I shall teach you the three kinds of persons. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would explain to me the meaning of this statement. “Then listen, Ānanda, and attend closely. I shall speak. “Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Ānanda, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three?

The person who is like a young, tender lotus flower, the person who is like a mature lotus flower, and the person who is like a withered lotus flower. And how, Ānanda, is a person like a young, tender lotus flower? Here, Ānanda, a certain person is a trainee (sekha) who has not yet attained final knowledge (aññā), who dwells aspiring for the unsurpassed security from bondage, and who possesses the five faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. This, Ānanda, is called a person like a young, tender lotus flower. And how, Ānanda, is a person like a mature lotus flower? Here, Ānanda, a certain person is an arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained the true goal, destroyed the fetters of existence, and is liberated through final knowledge. This, Ānanda, is called a person like a mature lotus flower. And how, Ānanda, is a person like a withered lotus flower? Here, Ānanda, a certain person is one who has committed an immediate offense (ānantariya-kamma), who has abandoned the training and returned to the lower life, or who has died with a mind full of hatred. This, Ānanda, is called a person like a withered lotus flower. These, Ānanda, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is wonderful, it is marvelous! How well this has been stated by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, I shall teach you the three kinds of persons. “It is because of this very reason, Ānanda, that this was said by me: ‘Monks, I shall teach you the three kinds of persons. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, the venerable Ānanda delighted in the words of the Blessed One. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. Thereupon, the venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him: “Venerable sir, it was said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, I shall teach you the three kinds of persons. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would explain to me the meaning of this statement. “Then listen, Ānanda, and attend closely. I shall speak. “Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Ānanda, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a young, tender lotus flower, the person who is like a mature lotus flower, and the person who is like a withered lotus flower. And how, Ānanda, is a person like a young, tender lotus flower? Here, Ānanda, a certain person is a trainee who has not yet attained final knowledge, who dwells aspiring for the unsurpassed security from bondage, and who possesses the five faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. This, Ānanda, is called a person like a young, tender lotus flower. And how, Ānanda, is a person like a mature lotus flower? Here, Ānanda, a certain person is an arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained the true goal, destroyed the fetters of existence, and is liberated through final knowledge. This, Ānanda, is called a person like a mature lotus flower. And how, Ānanda, is a person like a withered lotus flower? Here, Ānanda, a certain person is one who has committed an immediate offense, who has abandoned the training and returned to the lower life, or who has died with a mind full of hatred. This, Ānanda, is called a person like a withered lotus flower. These, Ānanda, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is wonderful, it is marvelous! How well this has been stated by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, I shall teach you the three kinds of persons. “It is because of this very reason, Ānanda, that this was said by me: ‘Monks, I shall teach you the three kinds of persons. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, the venerable Ānanda delighted in the words of the Blessed One.
The Second Discourse on the Taints.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
The taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance—
these, monks, are the three taints.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
With regard to this, it is said:
“For one whose taint of sensual desire is exhausted...”
the taint of existence is utterly exhausted;
he is completely liberated, free from acquisitions.
“He bears his final body, having conquered Māra and his host.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
